newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cutting back staff at Sierra Leone embassy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cutting back staff at Sierra Leone embassy.

text.p: The United States said on Wednesday it was cutting the number of American personnel at its embassy in Sierra Leone and making plans for an emergency evacuation if needed following a weekend military coup there.
"The Department of State has ordered a drawdown of United States embassy non-essential personnel and dependents," department spokesman John Dinger told reporters.
"Contingency plans for an emergency evacuation, should that prove necessary, are also being developed," Dinger added.

He said the U.S. Navy helicopter ship Kearsarge, which has been ordered to head towards Sierra Leone, was expected to arrive there late Wednesday or early Thursday to stand by in case an evacuation was ordered.
Dinger said the embassy drawdown "seems to be a prudent measure to take given the unsettled situation" in Sierra Leone.

He said there were about 40 Americans attached to the embassy in the capital Freetown. The department said Tuesday there were about 400 other Americans in the West African country, many of them aid workers and missionaries.
Military officers seized control Sunday in Sierra Leone, but regional power Nigeria landed hundreds of troops there Tuesday and is pressing for restoration of the civilian president.
The United States condemned the coup, and Dinger called again on the new Armed Forces Revolutionary Council to return power immediately to the elected government.

"The leaders of this coup need to understand that if they wish international support, if they wish for a true future of stability and prosperity for Sierra Leone, they have to reverse their action," he said.
Despite strong U.S. disapproval of the military government in Nigeria, Dinger said the Nigerians had been playing a "useful role" in Sierra Leone as leader of the regional peace force ECOMOG.
